scenes.tts: Chapter one asked of any pile: how fast does it arrive, and how fast does it leave? Now ask that inside the E R. What happens when unfinished proteins arrive faster than the E R can fold or remove them?
scenes.caption: Chapter 1 asked of any pile: how fast does it arrive, and how fast does it leave? Now ask that inside the ER. What happens when unfinished proteins arrive faster than the ER can fold or remove them?
scenes.visual: Open on chapter 1's full-cell recycling map (gray ER on the left, gold proteasome upper right, blue autophagosomes drifting to the large orange lysosome), with its two arrows 'arrival' and 'clearance' pulsing once. Then zoom into the gray ER until its lumen fills at least 70 percent of frame height. Gray client squiggles stream in from a slot on the ER boundary. On the right edge, a vertical gauge labelled 'unfolded load' appears and begins to creep upward. Label the gauge 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Chapter 1 asked of any pile: how fast does it arrive, and how fast does it leave? Now ask that inside the ER. What happens when unfinished proteins arrive faster than the ER can fold or remove them?

scenes.visual: Keep the ER lumen and the slowly rising gauge moving faintly. Dim slightly and show the title 'When the ER Falls Behind' over the center for 1.8 seconds, then restore full contrast.

scenes.tts: Many secreted and membrane protein chains enter the E R through a channel called the translocon. Chaperones then help them fold. BiP grips exposed hydrophobic stretches. Lectin chaperones read sugar tags on many glycoproteins, supporting repeated folding attempts. Folded clients can leave for the Golgi.
scenes.caption: Many secreted and membrane protein chains enter the ER through a channel called the translocon. Chaperones then help them fold. BiP grips exposed hydrophobic stretches. Lectin chaperones read sugar tags on many glycoproteins, supporting repeated folding attempts. Folded clients can leave for the Golgi.
scenes.visual: A gray squiggle threads in through a slot in the ER boundary; label the slot 'translocon' once the chain is through. A teal block labelled 'BiP' clamps onto a bumpy segment of the squiggle. A small green sugar flag appears on another client; a second teal block labelled 'lectin chaperone' grabs the flag, lets go, and grabs again, tracing chapter 1's looped arrow. Morph one folded client into a simple rounded blob and let it exit on the top edge toward a pale violet stack labelled 'Golgi'. A green exit arrow there is labelled 'exit 1: folded'.
scenes.narration: Many secreted and membrane protein chains enter the ER through a channel called the translocon. Chaperones then help them fold. BiP grips exposed hydrophobic stretches. Lectin chaperones read sugar tags on many glycoproteins, supporting repeated folding attempts. Folded clients can leave for the Golgi.

scenes.tts: Some persistently misfolded clients enter E R associated degradation, or E RAD. During return toward the cytosol, yeast H R D one adds a ubiquitin chain. C D C forty eight extracts the tagged client for destruction by the proteasome.
scenes.caption: Some persistently misfolded clients enter ER-associated degradation, or ERAD. During return toward the cytosol, yeast Hrd1 adds a ubiquitin chain. Cdc48 extracts the tagged client for destruction by the proteasome.
scenes.visual: One squiggle cycles repeatedly through the chaperone loop but stays tangled; show no fixed tally or cutoff. It is selected for ERAD and begins moving into a dashed passage beside a block labelled 'Hrd1 (yeast)'; a small '?' marks the proposed passage. As part of the client emerges on the cytosolic side, a chain of red ubiquitin tags grows there. A simple gold block labelled 'Cdc48' pulls the tagged client fully out and passes it to chapter 1's gold proteasome barrel, where it straightens and is cut into short pieces. A red exit arrow is labelled 'exit 2: ERAD'. No molecular structures.
scenes.narration: Some persistently misfolded clients enter ER-associated degradation, or ERAD. During return toward the cytosol, yeast Hrd1 adds a ubiquitin chain. Cdc48 extracts the tagged client for destruction by the proteasome.

scenes.tts: Now count the flows. Arrival is E R destined chains entering. Clearance is folding and export, plus removal by E RAD. When chains arrive faster than both exits can take them, unfolded proteins build up. The E R senses that stress and raises an alarm.
scenes.caption: Now count the flows. Arrival is ER-destined chains entering. Clearance is folding and export, plus removal by ERAD. When chains arrive faster than both exits can take them, unfolded proteins build up. The ER senses that stress and raises an alarm.
scenes.visual: Pull back so the whole ER is visible with three arrows: a thick gray 'arrival' arrow at the translocon, the green 'exit 1: folded' arrow and the red 'exit 2: ERAD' arrow. Thicken the arrival arrow; dots pile up inside the lumen and the 'unfolded load' gauge climbs past a dashed line. Plain-text equation on screen: 'load change = entry − (fold-and-export + ERAD)'. When the gauge crosses the line, a small amber bell on the ER membrane begins to pulse. Label the gauge and rates 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Now count the flows. Arrival is ER-destined chains entering. Clearance is folding and export, plus removal by ERAD. When chains arrive faster than both exits can take them, unfolded proteins build up. The ER senses that stress and raises an alarm.

scenes.tts: This alarm is the unfolded protein response. Look at the equation. Which flows could the response change to bring the load down?
scenes.caption: This alarm is the unfolded protein response. Look at the equation. Which flows could the response change to bring the load down?
scenes.visual: Label the pulsing amber bell 'unfolded protein response (UPR)'. Keep the three arrows and the gauge above the dashed line. Put the question 'Which flows could it change?' across the top. Circle each arrow in turn with a faint white outline: arrival, then fold, then remove. Dots keep drifting in the lumen.
scenes.narration: This alarm is the unfolded protein response. Look at the equation. Which flows could the response change to bring the load down?

scenes.visual: Hold the predict frame and the question for 4.5 seconds. Only the lumen dots drift and the bell pulses softly; do not change any arrow.

scenes.tts: It can change both sides. In mammals, a sensor called PERK slows the making of most new proteins, so less arrives. The response also increases folding helpers and removal machinery. Less in and more out let the load fall.
scenes.caption: It can change both sides. In mammals, a sensor called PERK slows the making of most new proteins, so less arrives. The response also increases folding helpers and removal machinery. Less in and more out let the load fall.
scenes.visual: From the bell, an amber line runs to the arrival arrow, which thins; label it 'PERK: slower synthesis'. Then more teal chaperone blocks appear in the lumen and the green and red exit arrows thicken; label them 'more helpers' and 'more removal'. The 'unfolded load' gauge falls back below the dashed line. Keep 'schematic' on the gauge.
scenes.narration: It can change both sides. In mammals, a sensor called PERK slows the making of most new proteins, so less arrives. The response also increases folding helpers and removal machinery. Less in and more out let the load fall.

scenes.tts: Mammals have three branches. I R E one splices the X B P one message. PERK slows translation. A T F six travels to the Golgi, where proteases release its transcription factor domain. Yeast relies on one E R stress sensor, Ire one.
scenes.caption: Mammals have three branches. IRE1 splices the XBP1 message. PERK slows translation. ATF6 travels to the Golgi, where proteases release its transcription factor domain. Yeast relies on one ER-stress sensor, Ire1.
scenes.visual: Split the amber bell into three labelled amber blocks spanning the ER membrane: 'IRE1', 'PERK', 'ATF6'. IRE1: a line of mRNA (a flat ribbon labelled 'XBP1 mRNA') loses a short highlighted segment, and the ribbon rejoins. PERK: the arrival arrow thins again. ATF6: the block buds off in a small vesicle to the violet Golgi stack, where scissors icons cut it and a fragment heads toward a nucleus outline. Then a small inset in the corner: a yeast cell with one amber block labelled 'Ire1'. Blocks and ribbons only.
scenes.narration: Mammals have three branches. IRE1 splices the XBP1 message. PERK slows translation. ATF6 travels to the Golgi, where proteases release its transcription factor domain. Yeast relies on one ER-stress sensor, Ire1.

scenes.tts: The response buys time, but has limits. Persistent stress can also drive cell death. The E R can retry clients, remove them, slow arrival, or raise capacity. These moves rebalance arrival and clearance. When folding falls behind, reduce arrival and expand capacity.
scenes.caption: The response buys time, but has limits. Persistent stress can also drive cell death. The ER can retry clients, remove them, slow arrival, or raise capacity. These moves rebalance arrival and clearance. When folding falls behind, reduce arrival and expand capacity.
scenes.visual: Run the gauge up and keep it high above the dashed line for a long stretch; the ER outline dims and a small gray 'cell death' label fades in beside the cell edge, marked 'if stress persists'. Fade out that stressed example, then restore the earlier balanced ER as a recap rather than a recovery. Pulse four labels in turn on established objects: 'retry' on the chaperone loop, 'remove' on the ERAD route, 'slow arrival' on the entry arrow and 'raise capacity' on the amber sensors. Zoom back out to chapter 1's full-cell map, highlighting the arrival and clearance arrows.
scenes.narration: The response buys time, but has limits. Persistent stress can also drive cell death. The ER can retry clients, remove them, slow arrival, or raise capacity. These moves rebalance arrival and clearance. When folding falls behind, reduce arrival and expand capacity.

scenes.visual: Fade the map to a dark outline while the ER's arrival and exit arrows pulse slowly. Center the end-card line in large white text: 'When folding falls behind, reduce arrival and expand capacity.'
